Quick answer: Jetpack is a free WordPress plugin made by Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com. The free version adds site stats, downtime alerts, brute-force login protection, an image CDN, a newsletter and automatic social sharing. The paid plans add real-time backups, malware scanning, a firewall, spam protection and bigger limits. Most small sites should start free and pay only when they need reliable backups.

Key takeaways

  • The free plugin is genuinely useful: stats, downtime monitoring, login protection, an image CDN and social auto-sharing cost nothing.
  • Backups are the main reason to pay. Real-time, off-site backups with one-click restore are not in the free plan.
  • You can install single-purpose plugins instead (Jetpack Boost, Protect, Social, VaultPress Backup) if you only need one feature.
  • Jetpack needs a free WordPress.com account connection, and your site must be publicly reachable.
Quick pick

Want backups and security in one place? Compare Jetpack plans →

Disclosure from our own setup: ProSiteGuide runs Jetpack. We use Jetpack Social to auto-share new guides to our Facebook Page and LinkedIn, so parts of this review come from day-to-day use, not just the sales page.

What is Jetpack?

Jetpack is a plugin that connects your self-hosted WordPress site to Automattic’s cloud services. Some features run on Automattic’s servers (stats, the image CDN, backups, downtime checks), which is why you link the site to a free WordPress.com account during setup. Its WordPress.org listing shows millions of active installs, which makes it one of the most widely used plugins in the directory.

Jetpack is not a page builder or a theme. Think of it as a toolbox for security, performance, growth and site management, where you switch on only the modules you want.

What does the free Jetpack plugin include?

Jetpack’s pricing page lists features that “work the same on every plan,” and its free plan comparison sets the limits. The useful free features are:

Note the stats rule: the free plan covers personal sites. Jetpack’s plan table lists commercial-use stats in the paid plans, so a business site should read the current terms before relying on free stats.

What do the paid plans add?

The paid plans are where Jetpack becomes a security and backup service. On the pricing page in November 2026, the two all-in-one plans were:

Jetpack often runs first-year discounts (a 50% Black Friday offer was running when we checked), and the pricing page says plans renew at the regular price. Budget for the regular rate. Refunds are available within 14 days for yearly plans and 7 days for monthly plans, according to the pricing FAQ.

You can also buy single products. When we checked, VaultPress Backup started at $9.95/month regular (billed yearly), Jetpack Social’s paid tier was $9.95/month billed $119.40 yearly, and Jetpack Boost’s paid tier was $19.95/month billed $239.40 yearly.

Is Jetpack Backup worth paying for?

For most business sites, yes, if your host does not already give you reliable off-site backups. Jetpack’s VaultPress Backup saves changes in real time, stores copies on Jetpack’s servers (not your hosting account), and lets you restore to any point from the activity log with one click, even when the site is offline.

Check your host first. Many managed WordPress hosts include daily backups, and some (Pressable, for example) include Jetpack Security on every plan. Paying twice for backups is a common waste. Our website maintenance guide explains how often to test a restore, whichever tool you use.

Jetpack Boost and the image CDN: do they speed up your site?

They can help. The free Boost plugin optimizes CSS loading, defers non-essential JavaScript, caches pages and gives you performance scores. The paid tier automates critical CSS and adds performance history. The image CDN serves images from Automattic’s servers.

Speed still starts with good hosting and a light theme. Use Boost alongside the fixes in our Core Web Vitals guide, and avoid stacking two caching plugins (for example Boost page caching plus your host’s cache) without testing.

Jetpack Social: how we use it

Jetpack Social’s free tier auto-shares each new post to connected accounts when you publish, with a preview and an optional custom message. It supports Facebook, Instagram, Threads, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Nextdoor and Tumblr. The paid tier adds per-network custom messages and media, templates and a social image generator.

Our honest limitation from using it: an auto-share posts one image per post. If you want carousels or multi-image posts on Facebook, you still need Meta Business Suite.

Jetpack pros and cons

Who should use Jetpack?

  • Bloggers and small business sites on regular hosting: install the free plugin for stats, downtime alerts and social sharing.
  • Sites that take leads or orders: add real-time backups (VaultPress Backup or a plan that includes it) if your host does not back up off-site.
  • Sites already on a managed host with backups and a firewall: you may only need the free features.
  • Developers who prefer separate tools: pick the single-purpose plugins instead of the full plugin.

Spam is the other common reason to upgrade. Paid plans include Akismet, the anti-spam service from the same company; it is also sold on its own. Our essential WordPress plugins list and security plugin comparison show where Jetpack fits next to other options.

How to set up Jetpack in 5 steps

  1. In your dashboard go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Jetpack”, then install and activate it.
  2. Click “Set up Jetpack” and connect (or create) a free WordPress.com account.
  3. Choose the free plan to start. You can upgrade later from the Jetpack dashboard.
  4. Under Jetpack → Settings, switch on what you want: brute-force protection, downtime monitoring, the image CDN, stats.
  5. Under Jetpack → Social, connect your Facebook Page and LinkedIn so new posts share automatically.

FAQ

Is Jetpack free?

Yes, the core plugin is free. Backups, malware scanning, the firewall, Akismet spam protection, commercial stats and higher limits are paid.

Does Jetpack slow down WordPress?

Jetpack loads only the modules you turn on, and several of them (the image CDN, lazy loading, Boost) are meant to speed sites up. Test your pages in PageSpeed Insights before and after enabling features.

Do I need Jetpack if my host has backups?

Not necessarily. If your host keeps daily off-site backups you can restore yourself, Jetpack Backup is optional. It adds real-time backups and a restore that works even if the host has an outage.

Can I use Jetpack on WordPress.com?

WordPress.com sites already include many Jetpack features as part of their plans. The plugin is mainly for self-hosted WordPress.org sites.

Is Jetpack safe?

Jetpack is built by Automattic and is one of the most installed plugins on WordPress.org. As with any plugin, keep it updated.

Verdict: is Jetpack worth it?

Install the free plugin. Its stats, downtime alerts, login protection and social sharing are worth having on almost any WordPress site. Pay for a plan when you need off-site, real-time backups and malware scanning that your host does not already provide, and compare the regular renewal price, not the first-year discount. Prices and features were checked on the vendors’ official pages in November 2026. They change, so confirm on the vendor’s site before you buy.
